archive/limits#

Immutable archive admission policy.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let policy = ArchiveLimits(10, 1024, 4096, 255);
let active = policy.budget().entered("assets/icon.bin", 2);
let counted = active.expanded(2); // BEFORE retaining the actual bytes
let ready = counted.completed(); // total allowance remains spent

Description#

Immutable archive admission policy. All four bounds are positive, independent int values; validation order is entries, entry_size, total_size, path_length. Sizes count expanded payload bytes. Path length counts Unicode code points, including slashes, before ArchivePath validation/construction. No decoding, normalization, I/O, payload allocation or owned resources.

budget() issues independent immutable accounting. Callers retain successors; reusing an earlier value deliberately forks an independent budget. Format readers still must enforce this policy at admission/allocation boundaries. Raw input, metadata decoding and temporary codec memory need separate bounds.

object ArchiveBudget#

object ArchiveBudget

Serial entry accounting: idle -> entered -> expanded* -> completed -> idle. Entry admission checks phase, nonnegative declaration, remaining count, path, declared entry bytes and remaining total. Only count is spent at admission. Expanded chunks spend actual entry/total bytes BEFORE retention; headers are only early rejection hints. Declared/actual equality belongs to format parsers. Empty entries cost a slot; completing/draining never restores total/count. Compare before subtracting, so counters cannot wrap even at INT64_MAX.

expanded/completed/path/entry_remaining require an active entry. entered requires idle. Phase misuse is InvalidState; negative sizes are InvalidArgument. Failures leave the old value unchanged. No payload or stream is retained; only the active validated path is kept until completed().

Errors#

enum ArchiveLimitExceeded#

enum ArchiveLimitExceeded is Error = (detailed(limit is string, maximum is int))

Stable diagnostics retain the policy's original configured maximum, never a changing remaining count. Limits use entries/entry_size/total_size/path_length.
